plan.d: As TradingView does: Overview, Signal, Performance, Technicals, Valuation, Income statement, Profitability, Growth, Balance sheet, a new Cash flow group, Dividends, Latest quarter (the release group), Reporting, Ownership, Long run, Reactions. Group ids stay; moved fields go into FIELD_KEY_MOVED so saved tiles and phone setups follow them.

plan.t: One period a column, said in its header
plan.d: A period tag on every header, TradingView-style: TTM, Q YoY, Q end, Now, Fwd. The group banner says the group’s period too (Income statement · TTM). Display text only; stored keys keep their names. A per-column period selector, as TradingView has, is a larger build and is left out.

plan.t: Half-yearly reporters on their own period
plan.d: Twelve months from the halves (the SEC data’s H and FY rows already allow it) and growth on the half a year earlier, marked as half-yearly in the hover, instead of a quarter they do not report.
Twelve months, by the owner’s rule; Twelve Data’s is mostly one quarter’s. Not a Signal input.

plan.t: Statement figures by the owner’s rule
plan.d: The release while it is the newest, the SEC data once it has the quarter and is dependable (restatements included), Twelve Data where neither is (docs/context/data-sources.md). Each row shows what the rule would use today. Display first; Signal inputs wait for the owner.

plan.t: Decide the free cash flow measure
plan.d: Levered (Twelve Data) or operating cash flow less capex (the filings). Three columns and two Signal inputs follow it.
Current and long-term borrowings, leases apart, from the filings. Needs the missing debt lines extracted.
Operating income, capex, interest cover (from data already stored); EBITDA margin, ROIC and FCF per share once their new data is extracted. Listed below.
Highlighted in the table and listed below: most are SEC concepts (no API credits), one is a release field.

tradingview.d: Twelve column sets: Overview, Performance, Technicals, Extended hours, Forecasts, Valuation, Dividends, Profitability, Income statement, Balance sheet, Cash flow, Per share. A reader finds a figure where the financial statements put it.

tradingview.t: Every financial column carries its period
tradingview.d: Fields are named by period (total_revenue_ttm, _fq for the fiscal quarter, _fh for the fiscal half, _fy for the year, price_earnings_current, dividend_amount_upcoming), and each screener column has a period selector: TTM, quarterly, semiannual, annual.
The _fh fields keep companies that report twice a year (foreign filers such as Rio Tinto) on a period they actually report, rather than a quarter they do not have.

tradingview.t: Forecasts are a set of their own
tradingview.d: Estimates (EPS, revenue, EBITDA, free cash flow, next twelve months) sit apart from reported figures, so a forward number is never read as a reported one.
Operating income, EBITDA and its margin, capex, ROIC, interest cover and per-share and per-employee versions sit beside the headline lines.
